2024-09-30.basis: The November 7 earnings release was the earliest qualifying public disclosure found. For the three months ended September 30, 2024, Molson Coors reported consolidated GAAP net sales after excise taxes of $3,042.7 million, down 7.8% from $3,298.4 million a year earlier. The 95% cutoff was $3,133.48 million. The August call anticipated a Q3 shipment decline but gave no upper bound for consolidated Q3 net sales.

coverage.detail: The original Q3 2023 statement of operations reported net sales of $3,298.4 million. That matches the comparative in the Q3 2024 release, confirming the denominator was unchanged.
April 30 Q1 release reaffirmed full-year 2024 top-line growth guidance. It supplied no Q3 reported net-sales point or range.

On the April 30 call, management expected excess U.S. shipments to reverse over the next nine months, mostly in the second half. The estimate was in hectoliters and did not establish Q3 consolidated revenue.
At the June 5 Deutsche Bank conference, management discussed softer April and May industry trends and reaffirmed its growth outlook. It gave no qualifying Q3 sales bound.

The August 6 Q2 release reported Q2 net sales of $3,252.3 million and retained guidance for a low-single-digit full-year net-sales increase in constant currency. It gave no Q3 reported revenue ceiling.
The August 6 earnings presentation covered Q2 performance and full-year guidance. It contained no qualifying Q3 consolidated net-sales forecast.

The August 6 call gave the clearest advance Q3 indication. U.S. shipments exceeded retail sales by about 1.1 million hectoliters across Q1 and Q2, with most of the reversal expected in Q3. Management also expected over half the roughly 1 million remaining Pabst hectoliters to exit in Q3. Neither volume estimate set a dollar or percentage bound on consolidated net sales.

The issuer's investor-event archive lists the August 6 and November 7 earnings calls consecutively. It lists no intervening investor conference or presentation. The May 15 annual meeting entry links the proxy statement only.

The issuer's September 16 public recap of its San Antonio distributor convention described commercial priorities for 2025 and beyond. It gave no Q3 consolidated sales forecast. A full public convention transcript was not located.
The October 7 notice scheduled the November 7 Q3 call. It disclosed no preliminary results or updated Q3 guidance.
The intervening October 18 Form 8-K concerned the resignation of the EMEA&APAC chief executive. It contained no Q3 sales update.
The November 7 issuer release gives both quarterly amounts in its consolidated statement of operations and identifies the 7.8% decline in the reported column.

The November 8 Form 10-Q confirms both amounts. It records the U.S. craft-business disposals within Americas operating results, including a $41.1 million disposal loss. The reported comparison requires no pro forma adjustment.
EDGAR records acceptance of the Q3 earnings Form 8-K on November 7 at 06:33:47, before the scheduled 8:30 a.m. Eastern earnings call.

2024-09-30.publication_date_evidence: The issuer's IR release and SEC Exhibit 99.1 both carry the November 7, 2024 dateline. EDGAR independently confirms same-day acceptance of the earnings release as an exhibit to the Item 2.02 Form 8-K.

The 95% threshold was $2,466.58 million. The reported decline was 11.3%. Earlier management comments identified Q1 shipment headwinds but supplied no upper bound for consolidated reported net sales.

coverage.detail: November 7, 2024 Q3 release. The revised sales outlook was an approximate 1% constant-currency decline for full-year 2024. The quarterly shipment estimate concerned U.S. wholesaler and retailer volumes in Q4 2024.
November 7 call. Management discussed the Pabst contract wind-down carrying into 2025 and referred investors to the Q4 call for 2025 guidance. It gave no Q1 2025 consolidated sales figure.

December 3 Morgan Stanley Global Consumer & Retail Conference. Management discussed brand performance and declined to forecast the 2025 industry environment. The discussion supplied no Q1 consolidated revenue bound.
February 13, 2025 Q4 release. Management projected low-single-digit net sales growth for full-year 2025 on a constant-currency basis. It gave no quarterly reported-sales range.

February 13 presentation, slides 15–16. The sales target was annual. The Q1-specific disclosure concerned the comparison with elevated U.S. demand and distributor inventory built ahead of the prior-year Fort Worth strike.

February 13 call. The CFO quantified approximately 1.9 million hectoliters of 2025 Americas volume headwind from exiting Pabst and Labatt contracts. She said the Pabst comparison was particularly pronounced in Q1. Neither the volume estimate nor the shipment timing established a quarterly consolidated dollar amount.

February 19 CAGNY presentation and Q&A. Asked about annual currency-neutral sales guidance, the CEO discussed Pabst headwinds over three quarters, Labatt over the year, pricing and incremental Fever-Tree sales. He gave no Q1 reported-sales point or range.

The original Q1 2024 release reported $2,596.4 million of consolidated net sales, matching the comparative in the May 2025 release. 2024-12-31.basis: Mesa’s fiscal Q1 2025 earnings release was the earliest qualifying issuer communication found. coverage.detail: The original fiscal Q1 2024 release reports $118,777,000 for October–December 2023. The fiscal Q1 2025 comparative preserves that amount, so no revenue restatement or perimeter adjustment is needed.

October 16, 2024, fiscal Q3 2024 release. The $110.8 million revenue figure covers the June quarter. Management discussed higher United block-hour rates, fleet transition timing and up to $14 million of transition reimbursements. None sets a December-quarter consolidated revenue ceiling.

The January 7, 2025 current report disclosed the December 31 agreement to sell 18 E-175 aircraft to United, with closings spanning December and January. Aircraft-sale proceeds do not establish quarterly operating revenue.

February 14 late-filing notice for the exact quarter. Mesa said it needed time to finalize its statements, checked No on the significant-change question in Part IV(3), and supplied no preliminary revenue amount or range.
The subsequent Nasdaq notice concerned the delinquent December 10-Q and September 10-K. It addressed filing compliance without quantifying December revenue.

April 7 merger announcement. The approximately $1.5 billion revenue figure belongs to Republic for 2024. The release and management remarks provide no stand-alone Mesa revenue figure for October–December.

May 14, immediately preceding earnings release. The $115.3 million actual covers fiscal Q4 ended September 30, 2024. December disclosures include 8.9 daily block hours and aircraft transactions, with no consolidated revenue point or range. Neither this release nor the October 16 release announced an earnings call. Searches identified no separate public call, investor presentation or management meeting for either release, or intervening public remarks giving a qualifying bound.
The other May 14 late-filing notice concerns the quarter ended March 31, 2025. It supplies no December-quarter revenue bound.

EDGAR records Friday, May 16 at 18:10:08 as the 10-Q acceptance time and Monday, May 19 as the filing date.

The SEC explains that ordinary submissions transmitted after 5:30 p.m. ET receive next-business-day dissemination. Form 10-Q falls under this rule. The Friday acceptance therefore does not advance the public date.

2024-05-04.basis: Buckle’s April sales release reported actual net sales for the full 13-week fiscal first quarter ended May 4, 2024. Sales fell 7.2% from the prior-year quarter ended April 29, 2023. The November 17 management call reiterated Buckle’s policy against issuing future sales or earnings guidance. The dated call transcript contains no qualifying fiscal Q1 2024 sales figure.
March 7. February net sales fell 5.2% to $78.2 million. The figure covered only the first four weeks of fiscal Q1.
March 15, immediately previous earnings release. Buckle reported $382.4 million for the 14-week fiscal Q4 ended February 3. It gave no fiscal Q1 2024 consolidated sales point or range.
The March 15 fiscal Q4 call again stated the policy against future sales or earnings guidance. No fiscal Q1 sales bound appeared in the transcript.
March 21. The intervening 8-K announced the departure of the head of women’s merchandising and gave no quarterly sales update.
March 26. The public disclosure from the March 25 board meeting announced a $0.35 quarterly dividend and gave no sales outlook.

The April 11 management commentary covered monthly merchandise and transaction trends and expressly reiterated the policy against guiding current sales or projecting next-quarter results.

The April 19 proxy scheduled the annual shareholder meeting for June 3, after both sales and earnings had been released. The earlier-disclosure search identified no intervening public investor presentation or additional management meeting giving a fiscal Q1 revenue bound.
May 9. The second paragraph explicitly reported the entire quarter’s net sales of $262.5 million against $282.8 million, down 7.2%. This was the first qualifying disclosure.
May 24 earnings release, Exhibit 99.1. Its income statement reported sales net of returns and allowances of $262,480 thousand against $282,834 thousand.
The June 13 Form 10-Q confirmed both figures in the condensed consolidated statements of income for the paired 13-week quarters.

2024-09-30.basis: ArcBest’s November 1 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated GAAP statements of operations report revenue of $1,063,124,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2024, versus $1,128,350,000 a year earlier. Revenue fell 5.78065% and was $8,808,500 below the $1,071,932,500 cutoff. The earlier quarterly guidance covered segment operating performance and did not set an upper bound on consolidated revenue.

coverage.detail: April 30, preceding earnings cycle. Exhibits 99.1–99.3 contain the Q1 release, supplemental information and call slides. The supplement reported preliminary April segment statistics and discussed historical Q1-to-Q2 operating-ratio changes. It gave no Q3 consolidated sales forecast.

April 30 call, checked through a third-party transcript. In Q&A, management discussed Q3 tonnage and shipment comparisons. The CFO characterized the operating-ratio figures as historical context and said more detail would follow closer to Q3.
June 7 business update. Quarter-to-date figures covered April and May. The update addressed Q2 segment trends and supplied no Q3 consolidated revenue bound.
August 2, immediately preceding earnings release. Exhibit 99.1 reported $1.08 billion of Q2 revenue from continuing operations. Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 supplied the outlook and call presentation.

August 2 guidance anticipated lower year-over-year Q3 Asset-Based daily tonnage, an Asset-Based operating ratio consistent with Q2, and a comparable Asset-Light operating loss excluding contingent-consideration changes. The 10% decline in Asset-Light revenue per day covered July alone.

August 2 call, checked through a third-party transcript. Management discussed July daily revenue, Q3 tonnage and segment profitability. No full-quarter consolidated revenue point or range was identified. The April and August call checks used published transcripts alongside the issuer’s filed call materials.

The Q2 investor presentation supplied historical financial results, strategy and operating metrics. It contained no qualifying Q3 consolidated revenue outlook. The search identified no separate intervening public investor meeting with quarter-specific revenue guidance.

September 3 was the closest earlier candidate. For July and August combined, Asset-Based billed revenue per day fell 3% and Asset-Light revenue per day fell 7% year over year. Workday counts differed, August was preliminary, and Asset-Based billings excluded the GAAP deferral adjustment for undelivered freight. The full-Q3 ranges covered the Asset-Based operating ratio and an approximately $5 million to $6 million non-GAAP Asset-Light operating loss. None established a full-quarter consolidated sales ceiling.
September 26 public announcement. The Regulation FD disclosure concerned the chief innovation officer’s retirement and succession.
October 1. ArcBest scheduled the Q3 results release for November 1 before market open. The notice supplied no preliminary sales figure.
October 30. The 8-K announced a $0.12 quarterly cash dividend and supplied no Q3 revenue figure.

The original Q3 2023 release reported $1,128,350,000 of consolidated revenue from continuing operations, matching the comparative in the 2024 release. ArcBest sold FleetNet on February 28, 2023, before both comparison quarters.

The Q3 2024 Form 10-Q corroborates both quarterly GAAP amounts. The change to prior-year Asset-Light operating statistics for managed transportation left the consolidated revenue denominator unchanged.

2024-03-31.basis: Ingredion’s May 8 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its condensed consolidated statements of income report GAAP net sales of $1,882 million for the three months ended March 31, 2024, versus $2,137 million a year earlier. The decline was 11.93%, and the reported amount was below the $2,030.15 million cutoff. The February 6 forecast of a mid-single-digit decline allowed for a decline smaller than 5%.

coverage.detail: The original Q1 2023 consolidated income statement reported $2,137 million of net sales. The 2024 segment recast preserved that consolidated denominator.
The November 7, 2023 Q3 release forecast mid-single-digit net sales growth for full-year 2023. It gave no Q1 2024 consolidated sales point or range.
The November 7 call discussed the planned Q1 2024 reorganization and margin prospects. Neither the call nor its earnings presentation supplied a Q1 2024 consolidated sales bound.
The February 1 closing announcement quantified the consideration for the South Korea business. It gave no consolidated quarterly sales forecast.

On February 6, Ingredion explicitly forecast Q1 2024 net sales to be “down mid-single-digits,” without a numeric endpoint. The 25–35% decline range applied to operating income. The separate full-year sales outlook excluded the South Korea divestiture.

On the February 6 call, CFO Jim Gray confirmed Q1 2023 as the comparison and described a mid-single-digit sales decline. Neither the call nor the accompanying earnings slides established a minimum 5% sales decline.

The February 21 CAGNY slides and management transcript were both available. Management gave full-year sales outlooks for the company and its new segments and discussed the Q1 peso impact. It supplied no tighter Q1 consolidated sales bound. The search identified no other intervening material public investor presentation or call.
The February 27 intervening Form 8-K disclosed an executive resignation and contained no sales update.
The April 17 notice scheduled Q1 results for May 8 before market open. It disclosed no preliminary sales figure.

The 95% ceiling was $1,664,220,450. October guidance crossed that ceiling, and the December public management remarks supplied no lower upper bound.

July 29, 2024. The Q2 release guided consolidated net sales of $1.785 billion to $1.885 billion for Q3 2024. It gave no Q4 sales range.

October 28 Q3 release, Exhibit 99.1. Explicit Q4 2024 net-sales guidance was $1.60 billion to $1.70 billion. The high end exceeded the ceiling by $35,779,550.
Slide 12 of the October 28 earnings presentation shows the same $1.60 billion to $1.70 billion Q4 range.

On the October 28 call, the CEO explicitly identified $1.65 billion as the guidance midpoint. The CFO described that midpoint as an 11% sequential decline. Both figures left the $1.70 billion high end in place.
November 13. The 5% figure concerned an increase in the quarterly dividend. The release also announced a special dividend and gave no Q4 sales update.

November 19. Amkor identified two public December presentations, UBS and Nasdaq London, and announced availability for one-on-one and small-group meetings. No public record of those private discussions was identified.

December 3 UBS webcast. Asked to recap the existing outlook, CFO Megan Faust described the Q4 guide as down 11% sequentially, the same midpoint decline explained in October. December 16 Form 8-K. The Regulation FD disclosure and accompanying press release concerned John Liu’s board appointment. They supplied no quarterly sales guidance.
January 21, 2025. Amkor scheduled the February 10 after-market release and earnings call without providing preliminary sales.
February 10. The issuer’s release directly tabulates both December quarters in thousands of dollars. The $1,629,118,000 actual is the qualifying point, available before the February 21 Form 10-K.

coverage.detail: The original Q1 2024 earnings exhibit reported total operating revenues of $491,907,000 for the quarter ended March 30, 2024. That exact denominator also appears in the Q1 2025 comparative table.
The October 24, 2024 Q3 release reported historical results and announced the October 25 public call. It gave no Q1 2025 consolidated revenue range.
On the October 25 call, Beres guided to $450–475 million for Q4 2024 and $1.8–1.9 billion for full-year 2025. Neither range specified Q1 2025 revenue.

The February 6 release reported Q4 2024 revenue of $465,131,000. It gave no Q1 2025 revenue bound and invited investors to the February 7 call at 10:00 a.m. Eastern. The issuer advertised telephone replay access through February 14. I verified the forecast in the public call transcript.

The March 17 Form 10-K reported annual results and separate pro forma acquisition figures. It supplied no revised Q1 consolidated revenue bound.

The 8-K records the April 23 shareholder meeting and identifies April 24 as the public earnings-release date. I located the meeting’s voting results but no transcript of management remarks. The meeting occurred after the qualifying February call.

Quartr transcript of the original earnings call. The independent source audit checked the directly linked call recording against the original voice, including the $410 million upper bound.

February 20 preceding-cycle release. JBT forecast FY2024 revenue of $1.750–$1.780 billion and approximately 47% in the first half. Neither establishes a Q2 upper bound.
February 21 earnings call. The issuer archive lists the release, slides and 10-K. Its slide link returned a cache miss. The event page yielded no recording or transcript.

Recovered the full 17-page earnings deck from JBT’s original presentation host. Slide 8 forecasts approximately 47% of revenue in the first half and 53% in the second. The deck supplies no qualifying quarterly figure and does not cover the spoken Q&A.
JBT’s February call notice identifies the original conference and webcast hosts and says a replay would be available after the call.

The issuer-linked webcast returned a cache miss. May 2 Q1 call. The issuer-filed transcript covers management remarks and Q&A, including half-year organic growth, Q2 orders and a tax benefit. It supplies no qualifying consolidated Q2 revenue ceiling.

The proxy fixes the May 10 annual meeting at 9:30 a.m. Central, names Broadridge’s event URL and explicitly allows shareholder questions. JBT’s past-event calendar also lists the meeting at https://ir.jbtmarel.com/events/ir-calendar/past.

The meeting-specific URL yielded no readable event content. Its redirect, https://central.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/vsm/web?pvskey=JBT2024, displayed Broadridge’s general meeting directory. A dated archive request at https://web.archive.org/web/20240511/https://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/JBT2024 yielded no verifiable replay. I found no official transcript or slides covering the meeting remarks.
The May 14 Form 8-K confirms the May 10 meeting and reports three votes. It contains no record of management remarks or shareholder Q&A.
May 6 investor deck. The filed presentation covers JBT’s business, historical performance and proposed Marel combination. No qualifying Q2 revenue forecast found.
May 31 investor deck. The filed end-of-May presentation supplies no qualifying Q2 revenue point or range.

June 4 investor deck. The filed update covers operations and transaction progress. No qualifying Q2 revenue forecast found. JBT dates all three decks in its archive at https://ir.jbtmarel.com/events/presentations?page=3.
June 20 combination call. The filed transcript discusses $75 million of potential merger revenue synergies. It gives no standalone JBT Q2 revenue ceiling.
June 24 Iceland investor meeting. The 13-page issuer-hosted transcript covers the offer, synergies and investor questions. No standalone JBT Q2 revenue point or range found.
The intervening issuer releases cover the dividend, Marel offer and ESG report. The July 19 release announced the earnings schedule. The next listed release was the July 30 results.

The July 31 Form 10-Q confirms the June-quarter GAAP comparison. JBT reclassified prior-period AeroTech operations as discontinued after the sale. Marel’s tender offer was still open. Both quarterly revenue columns therefore cover JBT continuing operations before the Marel combination.

Item 2.02 confirms that JBT issued Exhibit 99.1 on July 30 for the quarter ended June 30. The exhibit’s three-month revenue row gives $402.3 million and $427.7 million at the table’s reported precision.

February 21 full management call and Q&A. Forecasts covered full-year growth of 5–7%, a seasonally smaller first quarter, and approximately 53% of annual sales in the second half. Q2 mentions included merger timing; no Q2 consolidated sales ceiling.
Proxy p.74 required a control number and share ownership on the record date to attend. No general-public route specified.
Issuer archive names the May 10 meeting without an available replay. The public earnings calls have separate archive pages.

Item 2.02 of the contemporaneous 8-K independently confirms issuance that day, and JBT’s press archive lists the same date. The July 31 10-Q corroborates the amounts. 2024-06-30.initial_review: July 30, 2024 is the earliest qualifying communication I verified. JBT reported consolidated GAAP revenue of $402.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2024, versus $427.7 million a year earlier. The decline was 5.94%, and the actual was $4.015 million below the $406.315 million cutoff. The date remains null because primary-source coverage of earlier oral remarks is incomplete, specifically the February 21 earnings call and May 10 shareholder meeting. The numeric fields describe the verified July 30 actual.

initial_review_coverage.detail: February 20, preceding earnings cycle. JBT forecast FY2024 revenue of $1.750–$1.780 billion, with approximately 47% in the first half. It described typical Q1 seasonality and gave no bounded Q2 sales forecast.

February 21 earnings call. JBT’s archived call page links the release, slides and 10-K. The slides repeat the approximate half-year split. I could not verify the complete spoken remarks and Q&A against an issuer recording or issuer-filed transcript.

May 1, immediately preceding release. JBT reported Q1 revenue of $392.3 million and guided to FY2024 revenue of $1.735–$1.765 billion, approximately 47% in the first half. Applying exactly 47% and subtracting Q1 gives an illustrative Q2 range of $423.15–$437.25 million, entirely above the cutoff. The approximate allocation supplied no binding quarterly endpoint.

May 2 Q1 call, including Q&A. The 47%/53% split prompted a question about half-year organic growth. Management discussed Q2 orders, warehouse automation and a discrete tax benefit. None supplied a consolidated Q2 revenue ceiling.

JBT’s archive dates the Q1 slides May 1 and the intervening standalone investor decks May 6, May 31 and June 4. The investor decks presented historical revenue, operating metrics and merger opportunities. I found no qualifying Q2 sales range in their SEC-filed versions.
May 10 annual shareholder meeting. The 8-K documents the votes. I could not verify a recording or transcript covering any management remarks or shareholder Q&A.
June 20 JBT–Marel combination call. The filed management transcript discusses $75 million of potential revenue synergies from the combination. It gives no qualifying standalone JBT Q2 revenue bound.
June 24 Iceland investor meeting. The issuer-filed transcript covers the takeover offer, expected synergies and investor questions. I found no standalone JBT Q2 GAAP revenue point or range.

The issuer’s intervening releases cover the dividend, Marel transaction and ESG report. The July 19 notice announced the earnings schedule. The next listed release was the July 30 actuals. I found no preliminary Q2 sales release in this sequence.

The Q2 10-Q confirms the comparable GAAP totals. Product and service revenue were $362.7 million and $39.6 million in 2024, versus $387.3 million and $40.4 million in 2023. Both periods exclude AeroTech, classified as discontinued starting in Q2 2023. The Marel offer was still pending, so both columns reflect JBT before the combination.
Item 2.02 confirms that JBT issued the Q2 results release on July 30. Its Exhibit 99.1 contains the consolidated income statement with both quarterly revenue figures.

2024-06-30.earlier_review_basis: July 30, 2024 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I verified. JBT’s consolidated income statement reports Q2 2024 revenue of $402.3 million versus $427.7 million in Q2 2023, a 5.94% decline. Revenue was $4.015 million below the $406.315 million cutoff.
